values.note: Bathhouses with hot showers; portable toilets. Early in the season the campground is rustic only, with no bathrooms, showers or running water.

facilities.source: https://ctparks.com/parks/american-legion-state-forest ('Bathhouses with hot showers, dishwashing, and potable water'; 'Dumping station'; 'Portable toilets available'; '*Early season is designated as rustic camping only - no bathrooms, showers or running water'), read 2026-11-11

values.note: 2026: Friday April 10 to Monday October 12 at noon. 2027: April 9 to October 11. Early season is rustic only, and DEEP says rustic camping is permitted in the off-season.

season.source: https://ctparks.com/parks/american-legion-state-forest ('2026 Season: Opens Friday, April 10 and closes Monday, October 12 at noon. 2027 Season: Opens Friday, April 9 and closes Monday, October 11 at noon.'; 'The camping season begins in mid-April and ends on Columbus Day, with rustic camping permitted during the off-season.'), read 2026-11-11

note: Pine woods along the West Branch Farmington River near Pleasant Valley, Barkhamsted. Sites 20 and 22 (north loop) and 5 (south loop) are the closest to the river, about 30-45 m away through the pines. One pet per site. --Claude
summary: ctparks + ReserveAmerica + campground map read: $17/$27 confirmed; 30 sites, no hookups, all 35 ft (14 pull-through); showers, water, dump, portable toilets; 2026 season Apr 10-Oct 12 written; riverfront supported by the official map for sites 20/22/5 (canopy hides the ground); phone found; note cleaned.
flags: WATERFRONT (stored riverfront, recommend keep with a caveat): DEEP's 2015 campground map puts sites 22, 20, 18 (north loop) and 1, 3, 5 (south loop) OUTSIDE the loop road on the river side, with nothing drawn between them and the West Branch Farmington River but trees. Measured on the map: site 22 ~30 m, 20 ~35 m, 5 ~40-45 m, 1 and 3 ~55-65 m from the river. ReserveAmerica tags 001, 005, 020 and 022 'Near Water' (all 35 ft RV sites; 020 and 022 pull-through). The river is ~30-40 m wide on imagery (riverfront, not creekside). Imagery (Esri, leafy) is continuous pine canopy, so it can neither confirm nor deny open ground; per the curation doc the official per-site map is primary. If the reviewer reads the pine woods as a continuous screen, the alternative is riverview.
